chose: strip the 'replaces rules verdict X' suffix from LLM label notes entirely; evidence.note is the model's note verbatim
over: keeping it but hiding it in the UI render layer
moving it to a separate structured evidence field
because: evidence.note is rendered to recipe readers who have no model of a rules classifier; the override fact is already machine-readable in method='llm:<provider>:<model>@vN', and prompt.ts already forbids the model from referencing the rule it overrides, so the merge layer was appending exactly what the prompt bans

chose: move the board-password invariant out of loadConfig into assertBoardSecured(), called only by server.ts before app.listen
over: declaring PIPELINE_AUTH_PASSWORD on pipeline-worker in railway.ts
skipping the guard when NODE_ENV=production but no PORT is bound
because: the invariant belongs to the process that serves the board, not to config parsing that both entrypoints share. Declaring the variable on the worker would satisfy the check by giving a UI-less process a UI password — the guard would still be wrong, just no longer loud. Placement before listen() keeps the original safety property: an unauthenticated board is never bound, not merely torn down after binding. NOTE: PR #49 reintroduces the same role-blind throw at plugins/env.ts:95 and must be fixed there too — its buildApp(role) already threads the role into every plugin's opts, so that fix is a role === 'server' condition.

written against a stale local main: it proposed assertBoardSecured() in services/pipeline/src/config.ts, but #49 had already merged and deleted that file. The generation actually deployed parses env in plugins/env.ts, so the fix landed there instead.

chose: scope the Bull Board password check to role === 'server' inside plugins/env.ts's parseEnv, defaulting an absent role to 'server'
over: declaring PIPELINE_AUTH_PASSWORD on pipeline-worker in railway.ts
a separate assertBoardSecured() called only from server.ts
defaulting an absent role to a non-server role
because: the invariant belongs to the process that serves the board, not to the env parsing all three roles share. app.ts already threads role into every plugin's opts, so the condition costs one argument and no new call site to forget. Giving the worker a password for a UI it does not have would silence the crash while leaving the guard wrong. Defaulting an unset role to 'server' keeps a bare register() in a test from becoming a way to skip the check. env has no plugin dependencies so it still loads before anything binds a port: an unauthenticated board is never reachable, not torn down after becoming reachable.

chose: declare DATABASE_URL on the pipeline service in railway.ts, matching the value set by hand to unbreak the crash
over: making DATABASE_URL optional in the env schema and failing lazily at first query
because: every role autoloads plugins/db.ts and plugins/env.ts requires the variable for all of them, so the server needs it to boot even though it runs no jobs. pg's Pool opens no socket until something queries, so an idle server costs postgres nothing. Declaring it also stops the next railway config apply from dropping the hand-set value.

chose: restore the migration as an empty tombstone file, keeping its name
over: deleting the kysely_migration ledger row in production
restoring the original COMMENT ON body
because: a migration that has run somewhere can be emptied but not unlinked; the ledger is append-only history. Emptying the body honors the AGENTS.md COMMENT ON ban without a destructive prod DB write, and without resurrecting the prose the ban removed.

chose: add services/pipeline/src/cli/backfill.ts — a wave-driven CLI that finally calls claimBatch/claimLlmBatch
over: a POST /backfill route on the pipeline server
because: resolves def-baa19d961a0e (the claim queries had no production caller). The claims are pure SELECTs with no cursor, so the loop must be: claim, enqueue, wait for backlog to fall, re-claim — convergence comes from work completing, and deterministic enrichJobId makes re-claims free. A CLI keeps a full-corpus reprocess an explicit operator act rather than something a schedule or an open HTTP route can start by accident.

chose: gate llm-enrich on the LLM_ENRICHMENT_ENABLED env var alone; delete the PostHog flag path
over: keeping the PostHog flag with the env var as an override in front of it
because: nothing about llm-enrich is user-facing: no session, no cohort, no experiment. The flag's only real feature was a percentage rollout over the recipe corpus, which backfill's --limit/--max already express directly, and it cost a network round trip plus a $feature_flag_called capture on the hot path of a queue that runs once per recipe. Left UNDECLARED in .railway/railway.ts (like the API keys) so railway config apply cannot clobber the operator's dashboard toggle; plugins/env.ts defaults it to "false" so unset is disabled.
